I'm confident that this fix resolves the issue described. The regex was missing a significant portion of the basic Latin alphabet, causing many strings to take the slow path in `set_cell_size`. Expanding the range from `\u006f` ('o') to `\u007e` ('~') fixes this for all printable ASCII characters.

I'll submit the patch now.

I have fixed the regex in `rich/cells.py` to include all printable ASCII characters, ensuring that strings containing characters from 'p' to 'z' (and other symbols) can use the fast path in `set_cell_size`. I verified the fix with a small script and ran the existing tests in `tests/test_cells.py`, which all passed.

The issue was caused by an incorrect regex in `rich/cells.py` used to identify strings consisting only of single-width characters. The regex `^[\\u0020-\\u006f\\u00a0\\u02ff\\u0370-\\u0482]*$` only included characters up to `\u006f` ('o'), meaning any string containing characters from 'p' to 'z' or other printable ASCII characters beyond 'o' would fail the check and fall back to a slower path in `set_cell_size`.

I updated the regex to `^[\\u0020-\\u007e\\u00a0\\u02ff\\u0370-\\u0482]*$`, expanding the range to `\u007e` ('~'), which covers all printable ASCII characters. This ensures that the fast path is correctly selected for a much wider range of common strings, improving performance.

Verified the fix by:
1. Testing the regex with strings containing characters beyond 'o' (e.g., "world").
2. Running `tests/test_cells.py` to ensure no regressions.
